html:
In the app

File → New Project… → A graded level → 13. Guided mode opens on this chapter: the tags, every rung below under its fold, a Verify check, and the run results: the axis is homed, a bottle is picked up, a bottle is set down in a bin, then complete, every bottle right and under par. File → Load Reference Solution loads the program printed here.

The axis chapter in Part VI (chapter 55) taught the FHPP handshake on a panel. This level puts it to work. Twelve bottles, small, medium and large, come down a short infeed one at a time. The belt ends under a servo axis standing across it: a Size 120 toothed-belt axis with a 4.5 m stroke and a vacuum gripper on its carriage. Three bins sit under the axis at 1500, 3000 and 4500 mm, one per size. Pick each bottle off the end of the belt, carry it to its bin, set it down, come back. The drive’s own rules are the level’s traps: no move before the axis is homed, no second Start while a move is running, and a bottle set down anywhere but over a bin is on the floor.

The machine

How the level is scored

What happensPoints
A bottle set down in its own bin+100
A bottle in the wrong bin−50
A bottle set down off the bins, or run off the end of the belt−50
Every drive fault at the end (a Start before Referenced, a record that is not set, a target past the stroke)−50 each
Every double start at the end (a Start while a move was running: the drive ignores it and raises Warning)−25 each
What happensPoints
All twelve bottles done under par (80 s)+200

The drive keeps the count: the axis properties show faults and double starts as you run, and the simulator log prints the Drive record line when the level completes.

The gripper

Grip is the vacuum. On its rising edge the gripper takes whatever bottle is under the carriage (Part_Below says there is one) and Gripped comes on; the bottle rides with the carriage and no eye, belt or bin sees it on the way. Drop Grip and the bottle is set down where the carriage is: into the bin under it, or onto the floor. Grip with nothing under the carriage does nothing but a line in the log. There is no Z axis here: the pick and the set-down are the vacuum alone, which is how a short-stroke vacuum pick on a gantry often is.

How to pass it, step by step

1. Power the drive with Run: Enable, Stop and Halt high, as in the axis chapter.

2. Home it before anything else, and only release bottles once Axis1:I.Referenced is on.

3. Run the belt until PE_Pick sees a bottle, then stop it, or the bottle runs off the end.

4. Latch the gantry beams as the bottle passes, as Level 1 did.

5. Grip when a bottle is at the pick point and the carriage is at rest at 0 mm. Pick the record from the

6. Over the bin, at rest: Grip off. Then record 1 and Start again, back to the pick point.

7. Drop Start when Start_Ack answers, every time.

Tags this lesson needs

The alias tags of the machine are made for you; create these before you type the rungs. Verify reports any you miss.

TagTypeKindDescription

Run, power and home

Rung 2 is the automatic home: while Run is on and the axis is not referenced, Home is held. The drive homes on Home’s rising edge and the rung drops out when Referenced comes back. XIO(Moving) and XIO(Fault) keep it from pulsing Home during a run or into a faulted drive.

Release, belt and gantry

Pick, record, out

The pick rung wants four things at once: a bottle at PE_Pick, Part_Below from the gripper, the carriage at rest (Motion_Complete) and at the pick point (Actual_Pos within 2 mm of 0: the drive reports hundredths of a millimetre, so 200). It latches Grip. Rung 8 turns the two latched beams into a record number while the bottle is held. Rung 9 starts the move, once, on the one-shot: Start stays latched until rung 12 drops it on the acknowledge.

Try it: a double start

Take the ONS(Out_ONS) out of rung 9. Now Start is latched every scan the rung is true, and the drive sees a second Start the moment Motion_Complete comes back over the bin, before rung 10 has let go of the bottle. The log says Start while moving: ignored (a double start), Warning comes on, and the drive record at the end costs 25 for each one.

Try it: start before homing

Take XIC(Axis1:I.Referenced) out of rung 3 and change rung 2 so Home never fires (delete it). The first bottle arrives, the gripper takes it, rung 9 starts the move, and the drive faults: positioning before homing. Op_Enabled drops, the fault lamp lights, nothing moves until Reset, and the bottle hangs in the gripper. Put rung 2 back, press Reset, and the home run takes the bottle with it to 0 mm, where the pick rung is already satisfied.

Set down, back, acknowledge

Rung 10 is the only place Grip is unlatched: at rest, past 1000 mm, holding a bottle. The bottle drops into the bin under the carriage on the next tick and Busy is unlatched in the same rung, so the hopper releases the next bottle while the axis is still on its way back. That overlap is where the par comes from: the book’s program does the twelve in about 65 s against a par of 80. Rung 11 sends the empty carriage back on record 1; XIO(Axis1:O.Start) keeps it from re-latching Start in the scan Start_Ack is dropping it.

The fault lamp and Reset

Run it

Load the program, Run mode, Start. The axis runs to its home switch at the pick point, the blue LED at the motor lights, the first bottle comes down, stops on PE_Pick, the gripper ring turns blue, and the carriage takes the bottle to its bin and comes back. 12 of 12 bottles in the right bin, nothing lost, in about 65 s against a par of 80 s: 1400 points and three stars.

rungs.head: Rung 0
rungs.comment: RUN: Start seals Run in; Stop or a tripped E-stop breaks it

pred.q: Start_PB is off, Run is on, Stop_PB is off and E_Stop is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Run is on.

rungs.words: When either (Start_PB (Start push button, momentary) is on) or (Run (Line running (sealed-in Start)) is on), Stop_PB (Stop push button, momentary) is off and E_Stop (E-stop, NC: 1 = healthy) is on, the rung turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Start_PB) Examine If Closed asks: true when Start_PB is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(Stop_PB) Examine If Open asks: true when Stop_PB is off.
  3. XIC(E_Stop) Examine If Closed asks: true when E_Stop is on.
  4. OTE(Run) Output Energize does: turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Run on, and Run’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.head: Rung 1
rungs.comment: POWER: with Run, the drive is enabled (CCON.B0), not stopped (CCON.B1) and not halted (CPOS.B0): Op_Enabled comes back
rungs.words: When Run (Line running (sealed-in Start)) is on, the rung turns Axis1:O.Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false), turns Axis1:O.Stop on (and off whenever the rung is false), turns Axis1:O.Halt on (and off whenever the rung is false) and turns Lamp_Run (Run lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. A branch of 4 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Axis1:O.Enable) Output Energize does: turns Axis1:O.Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTE(Axis1:O.Stop) Output Energize does: turns Axis1:O.Stop on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 3
    1. OTE(Axis1:O.Halt) Output Energize does: turns Axis1:O.Halt on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 4
    1. OTE(Lamp_Run) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 2
rungs.comment: HOME: the axis is not referenced yet, so home it before anything else; the only move the drive allows before Referenced

pred.q: Run is off, Axis1:I.Op_Enabled is off, Axis1:I.Referenced is on, Axis1:I.Moving is on and Axis1:I.Fault is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Axis1:O.Home is off. It stops at XIC(Run).

rungs.words: When Run (Line running (sealed-in Start)) is on, Axis1:I.Op_Enabled is on, Axis1:I.Referenced is off, Axis1:I.Moving is off and Axis1:I.Fault is off, the rung turns Axis1:O.Home on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIC(Axis1:I.Op_Enabled) Examine If Closed asks: true when Axis1:I.Op_Enabled is on.
  3. XIO(Axis1:I.Referenced) Examine If Open asks: true when Axis1:I.Referenced is off.
  4. XIO(Axis1:I.Moving) Examine If Open asks: true when Axis1:I.Moving is off.
  5. XIO(Axis1:I.Fault) Examine If Open asks: true when Axis1:I.Fault is off.
  6. OTE(Axis1:O.Home) Output Energize does: turns Axis1:O.Home on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 3
rungs.comment: RELEASE one bottle once the axis is homed and the last one is in its bin; forget the last height
rungs.words: When Run (Line running (sealed-in Start)) is on, Axis1:I.Referenced is on, Busy (A bottle is on the belt or in the gripper) is off, Infeed_Ready (Hopper exit clear: a bottle can be released) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung turns Infeed_Release (Release one bottle onto the belt (rising edge)) on (and off whenever the rung is false), latches Busy on, unlatches Is_Mid (The bottle broke the middle beam (medium or large)) and unlatches Is_High (The bottle broke the high beam (large)).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIC(Axis1:I.Referenced) Examine If Closed asks: true when Axis1:I.Referenced is on.
  3. XIO(Busy) Examine If Open asks: true when Busy is off.
  4. XIC(Infeed_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Infeed_Ready is on.
  5. ONS(Rel_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Rel_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  6. A branch of 4 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Infeed_Release) Output Energize does: turns Infeed_Release on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTL(Busy) Output Latch does: latches Busy on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 3
    1. OTU(Is_Mid) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Is_Mid. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 4
    1. OTU(Is_High) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Is_High. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: Busy stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: Rung 4
rungs.comment: BELT: run until a bottle reaches the pick point, then stop; a running belt would carry it off the end

pred.q: Run is on and PE_Pick is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Conveyor_Run is on.

rungs.words: When Run (Line running (sealed-in Start)) is on and PE_Pick (A bottle is at the end of the belt, under the axis at 0 mm) is off, the rung turns Conveyor_Run (Infeed belt motor) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(PE_Pick) Examine If Open asks: true when PE_Pick is off.
  3. OTE(Conveyor_Run) Output Energize does: turns Conveyor_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 5
rungs.comment: GANTRY: the middle beam is broken by medium and large bottles
rungs.words: When PE_Mid (Middle beam: medium and large) is on, the rung latches Is_Mid (The bottle broke the middle beam (medium or large)) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Mid) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Mid is on.
  2. OTL(Is_Mid) Output Latch does: latches Is_Mid on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Is_Mid stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 6
rungs.comment: the high beam by large only

pred.q: PE_High is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Is_High is left as it was. It stops at XIC(PE_High).

rungs.words: When PE_High (High beam: large only) is on, the rung latches Is_High (The bottle broke the high beam (large)) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_High) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_High is on.
  2. OTL(Is_High) Output Latch does: latches Is_High on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Is_High stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 7
rungs.comment: PICK: a bottle at the pick point, the carriage at rest within 2 mm of 0: gripper on (it stays on until the set-down)
rungs.words: When PE_Pick (A bottle is at the end of the belt, under the axis at 0 mm) is on, Part_Below (A bottle is under the carriage, within the gripper's reach) is on, Axis1:I.Motion_Complete is on and Axis1:I.Actual_Pos is at most 200, the rung latches Grip (Vacuum gripper on: picks the bottle under the carriage and holds it while 1) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Pick) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Pick is on.
  2. XIC(Part_Below) Examine If Closed asks: true when Part_Below is on.
  3. XIC(Axis1:I.Motion_Complete) Examine If Closed asks: true when Axis1:I.Motion_Complete is on.
  4. LEQ(Axis1:I.Actual_Pos,200) Less Than or Equal asks: true when Axis1:I.Actual_Pos is at most 200.
  5. OTL(Grip) Output Latch does: latches Grip on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Grip stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 8
rungs.comment: RECORD: with the bottle held, pick the bin by its height: record 2 small (1500 mm), 3 medium (3000), 4 large (4500)

pred.q: Gripped is on, Is_Mid is off and Is_High is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: Power reaches only part of the rung: Axis1:O.Record_No is written, Axis1:O.Record_No is not written (it keeps its value) and Axis1:O.Record_No is written.

rungs.words: When Gripped (The gripper holds a bottle) is on, each path is tested on its own: if Is_Mid (The bottle broke the middle beam (medium or large)) is off, it puts 2 into Axis1:O.Record_No; if Is_Mid is on and Is_High (The bottle broke the high beam (large)) is off, it puts 3 into Axis1:O.Record_No; if Is_High is on, it puts 4 into Axis1:O.Record_No.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Gripped) Examine If Closed asks: true when Gripped is on.
  2. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. XIO(Is_Mid) Examine If Open asks: true when Is_Mid is off.
    2. MOV(2,Axis1:O.Record_No) Move does: puts 2 into Axis1:O.Record_No. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Is_Mid) Examine If Closed asks: true when Is_Mid is on.
    2. XIO(Is_High) Examine If Open asks: true when Is_High is off.
    3. MOV(3,Axis1:O.Record_No) Move does: puts 3 into Axis1:O.Record_No. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 3
    1. XIC(Is_High) Examine If Closed asks: true when Is_High is on.
    2. MOV(4,Axis1:O.Record_No) Move does: puts 4 into Axis1:O.Record_No. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 9
rungs.comment: OUT: holding a bottle at the pick point, start the move to the bin; one shot, so the move is started once
rungs.words: When Gripped (The gripper holds a bottle) is on, Axis1:I.Motion_Complete is on, Axis1:I.Actual_Pos is at most 200 and this is the first scan of it, the rung latches Axis1:O.Start on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Gripped) Examine If Closed asks: true when Gripped is on.
  2. XIC(Axis1:I.Motion_Complete) Examine If Closed asks: true when Axis1:I.Motion_Complete is on.
  3. LEQ(Axis1:I.Actual_Pos,200) Less Than or Equal asks: true when Axis1:I.Actual_Pos is at most 200.
  4. ONS(Out_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Out_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  5. OTL(Axis1:O.Start) Output Latch does: latches Axis1:O.Start on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Axis1:O.Start stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Rung 10
rungs.comment: SET DOWN: at rest over a bin (past 1000 mm) with the bottle: gripper off, the bottle drops into the bin, the line is free for the next release
rungs.words: When Gripped (The gripper holds a bottle) is on, Axis1:I.Motion_Complete is on and Axis1:I.Actual_Pos is greater than 100000, the rung unlatches Grip (Vacuum gripper on: picks the bottle under the carriage and holds it while 1), unlatches Busy (A bottle is on the belt or in the gripper) and makes Pick_Count (Shown on the toolbar: bottles picked) = Pick_Count + 1.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Gripped) Examine If Closed asks: true when Gripped is on.
  2. XIC(Axis1:I.Motion_Complete) Examine If Closed asks: true when Axis1:I.Motion_Complete is on.
  3. GRT(Axis1:I.Actual_Pos,100000) Greater Than asks: true when Axis1:I.Actual_Pos is greater than 100000.
  4. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(Grip) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Grip. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Busy) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Busy. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 3
    1. ADD(Pick_Count,1,Pick_Count) Add does: makes Pick_Count = Pick_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Grip when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 11
rungs.comment: BACK: empty-handed over a bin: record 1 (0 mm) and start the move back to the pick point
rungs.words: When Gripped (The gripper holds a bottle) is off, Axis1:I.Motion_Complete is on, Axis1:I.Actual_Pos is greater than 100000 and Axis1:O.Start is off, each path is tested on its own: it puts 1 into Axis1:O.Record_No; if this is the first scan of it, it latches Axis1:O.Start on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Gripped) Examine If Open asks: true when Gripped is off.
  2. XIC(Axis1:I.Motion_Complete) Examine If Closed asks: true when Axis1:I.Motion_Complete is on.
  3. GRT(Axis1:I.Actual_Pos,100000) Greater Than asks: true when Axis1:I.Actual_Pos is greater than 100000.
  4. XIO(Axis1:O.Start) Examine If Open asks: true when Axis1:O.Start is off.
  5. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(1,Axis1:O.Record_No) Move does: puts 1 into Axis1:O.Record_No. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. ONS(Back_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Back_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
    2. OTL(Axis1:O.Start) Output Latch does: latches Axis1:O.Start on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Axis1:O.Start stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Rung 12
rungs.comment: ACK: the drive took the Start; drop it so the next Start is a new rising edge. A fault drops it too

pred.q: Axis1:I.Start_Ack is off and Axis1:I.Fault is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Axis1:O.Start is left as it was. None of the branch’s paths is true.

rungs.words: When either (Axis1:I.Start_Ack is on) or (Axis1:I.Fault is on), the rung unlatches Axis1:O.Start.
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Axis1:I.Start_Ack) Examine If Closed asks: true when Axis1:I.Start_Ack is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Axis1:I.Fault) Examine If Closed asks: true when Axis1:I.Fault is on.
  2. OTU(Axis1:O.Start) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Axis1:O.Start. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Axis1:O.Start when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 13
rungs.words: When Axis1:I.Fault is on, the rung turns Lamp_Fault (Fault lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Axis1:I.Fault) Examine If Closed asks: true when Axis1:I.Fault is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Fault) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Fault on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 14
rungs.comment: RESET: a fault clears on the rising edge of Reset

pred.q: Reset_PB is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Axis1:O.Reset is on.

rungs.words: When Reset_PB (Drive fault reset, momentary) is on, the rung turns Axis1:O.Reset on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Reset_PB) Examine If Closed asks: true when Reset_PB is on.
  2. OTE(Axis1:O.Reset) Output Energize does: turns Axis1:O.Reset on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

Busy.desc: A bottle is on the belt or in the gripper
